task_instance: Use the task-execution-engine to drive implementation of a small feature whose tasks live as markdown checkboxes in a design doc: I wrote a design doc with two tasks ('Create slug module' priority:1, and 'Add slug tests' priority:2 depending on the first), then ran the skill's execution loop (task_manager.py next -> implement -> verify -> done) until no tasks remained.
evidence: Copied the skill's bundled scripts/task_manager.py into the work dir and created docs/designs/2026-10-31-slugify.md with an '## Implementation Tasks' section containing two checkbox tasks (one with a deps: attribute). Ran with Python 3.13.17. 'status' reported Progress 0/2, Pending 1, Blocked 1 (the dependent task correctly blocked). 'next' returned 'Create slug module' with its files and 3 acceptance criteria. Implemented src/slug.py (slugify lowercases, replaces punctuation/spaces with hyphens, strips hyphens); verified all 3 criteria via inline asserts (hello-world | a-b-c | trim). 'done --task "Create slug module"' rewrote the markdown checkbox to [x] with the completion marker and checked its sub-criteria. 'next' then returned the previously-blocked 'Add slug tests' task (dependency resolution works). Wrote tests/test_slug.py; ran python3 -m pytest tests/test_slug.py -q -> '2 passed'. 'done' marked the second task complete. Final 'status' showed Progress 2/2 (100%), Completed 2, Pending/Blocked/Failed 0, and 'next' returned 'No pending tasks available'. The parse/next/done/status commands, priority ordering, dependency gating, markdown rewriting, and resume-from-markdown behavior all functioned as the skill specifies. Files produced: docs/designs/2026-10-31-slugify.md, src/slug.py, tests/test_slug.py, scripts/task_manager.py.
